articles.title: Poundland's future hangs in the balance as chain edges towards collapse
articles.description: Poundland's bosses is filing a notice of intention to appoint administrators to the business.
articles.summary: The future of Poundland hangs in the balance as the discount chain edges towards collapse, the BBC understands.
key_points: The retailer's bosses are filing a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which if approved by the High Court, will give the business 10 days breathing space to find a rescue deal.
The move comes after Poundland's managing director Barry Williams wrote a memo to his 12,000 staff across its 600 stores in the UK and Ireland saying the chains' US owner had limited Poundland's…
It is understood the firm's owner, Gordon Brothers, wants to break up the firm, with rivals Poundstretcher, B&M and Lidl interested in potentially buying up stores.

articles.title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules
articles.description: Campaigners had warned some families could face an unfair financial penalty because of delays which were not their fault.
articles.summary: Bereaved families will no longer be hit by an unexpected tax bill because of severe delays paying out civil service pensions, following a change in Wednesday's Budget.
key_points: Under previous HMRC rules, certain lump sum pension payments had to be paid within two years of the pension scheme being notified of a death to remain tax-free.
Campaigners had warned some families could face an unfair financial penalty because of delays which were not their fault.
The government has now changed the rules so payments will no longer become taxable solely because more than two years has passed.

articles.summary: Families facing cost-of-living pressures are being offered some help, or "breathing space" as Chancellor John Healey is calling it.
key_points: The help comes as prices are rising faster than expected with annual energy bills in particular likely to increase by hundreds of pounds in January.
Here's how the key announcements in the Budget affect you and your money.

articles.title: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17bn deal it says will expand customer options
articles.description: Instacart shoppers will be able to buy from 150,000 stores, compared to the 100,000 currently available on the platform, the firms said.
articles.summary: DoorDash will acquire grocery delivery firm Instacart in a $17bn (£12.8bn) deal, creating a behemoth that will bring more meals, quick-need purchases and big weekly shops directly to customers.
key_points: DoorDash said the deal, expected to be final in about a year, will expand options for customers and let more sellers use the companies' services.
Instacart shoppers will be able to buy from 150,000 stores, up from the current 100,000, while DoorDash will reach beyond restaurants into retail, the firms said.
"Together, we can accelerate innovation across the grocery industry and make online grocery more seamless and affordable for the millions of households we serve," Instacart's chief executive said.

Sanrio said it terminated its collaboration with Vivant after determining that it "contained elements inconsistent with Sanrio's core values".
